## Overview

With the Artemis II mission successfully paving the way for our return to deep space, a fascinating question emerged: *What is the absolute fastest humans have traveled each year, and how frequently have we shattered those limits?*

Looking at human velocity on a century-long time scale highlights an astonishing reality: for millennia, our speed boundary was tied directly to the stride of a horse. Within a mere handful of generations, that boundary shifted exponentially from steam power to aviation, jet propulsion, and eventually atmospheric escape.

## Technical Architecture & Data Prep

To reconstruct this historical timeline, I compiled and cross-verified historical velocity benchmarks using generative AI workflows, then isolated key architectural leaps. 

To maintain a clean layout for non-technical readers while keeping the core replication pipeline accessible, you can expand my underlying data preparation steps below.

::: {.panel-tabset}

### 🐍 Data Engineering Pipeline
{{< embed highest-human-speed.ipynb >}}

### 🛠️ Methodology Insights
* **Verification Loop:** Initial data structures generated via LLMs were cross-checked manually against aviation and aerospace records to ensure peak milestone accuracy (e.g., separating atmospheric jet records from low-Earth orbit velocities).
* **Scope:** The dataset normalizes peak vehicle speeds carrying human crews relative to the Earth's surface or orbital reference frames.
* **AI Tooling:** The base dataset was generated via Claude and double-checked for chronological anomalies using Gemini.
:::
